articles.title: Doom 2016 Composer Mick Gordon Says He'd Return to the Doom Series "In a Heartbeat"
articles.summary: Mick Gordon, the legendary Aussie composer who brought a headbang to every headshot in 2016's Doom and its 2020 follow-up Doom Eternal, has told IGN that he's open to the idea of contributing to future instalments in id Software's iconic shooter series.
body: "There are a lot of dominoes that would have to fall in a very specific way for that to occur," said Gordon. "If those dominoes ever fell in that way, I would. Of course. Within a heartbeat."

Gordon didn't elaborate on exactly what those "dominoes" might be, but it's possible that disputes between the composer and Doom Eternal's executive producer Marty Stratton have yet to be fully resolved. In a lengthy 2022 post on Medium, Gordon accused developer id Software of failing to pay him for half of his work on the Doom Eternal soundtrack, and singled out Stratton as being a recurringly abusive presence throughout his work on the score and the OST. However, it certainly seems as though the experience hasn't dimmed Gordon's love for Doom itself.
"I had a whole list of ideas where I wanted to go with Doom," explained Gordon. "And I'd love to explore that one day, for sure."

articles.title: Artemis Fowl Animated TV Show Greenlit With Eoin Colfer as Executive Producer
articles.summary: Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+. Author Eoin Colfer announced that Disney had greenlit another series project based on his family fantasy novels at the 25 Years of Artemis Fowl panel at New York Comic Con 2026.
body: Joining Colfer in the executive producing category is Marvel's Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur's Ben Juwono, as well as DuckTales' Colleen Evanson. In a statement, the Artemis Fowl author said he is "proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the Artemis Fowl animation on screen."
"Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands," he added.

The Artemis Fowl animated series has no release date, but when it does eventually arrive, it won't be the first swing at the property to land on Disney+. In 2020, Disney launched a live-action movie with the same name, though it largely failed to leave a good impression on fans or critics. As recorded by review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, the straight-to-streaming film only whipped up a "rotten" 8% from critics and 19% from audiences.

articles.title: 5 Exciting Games Stuck In Development For More Than 10 Years
articles.summary: However, some games get stuck in what is referred to in the industry as "development hell." Over the years, some of these have eventually been released, such as Duke Nukem Forever, Metroid Dread, and Skull & Bones.
body: Developing a competent video game is tough. Some games are such masterpieces that it's a wonder how they ever got made at all. There are so many moving parts, especially since studio sizes are often in the triple digits, that kudos needs to go to the games that are released despite going through various trials and tribulations.

When you saw the headline of this article, I have little doubt that Ubisoft’s Beyond Good & Evil 2 was the first game that you thought of. These days, it's the poster child for games trapped in development hell. It started pre-production in 2007, which means that it's been in the works for a whopping 19 years. While most studios would have canceled the project by now, Ubisoft confirmed as recently as January 2026 that the game is still being worked on, as six projects were canned; Beyond Good & Evil 2 was not one of them.
points: However, some games get stuck in what is referred to in the industry as "development hell.
Over the years, some of these have eventually been released, such as Duke Nukem Forever, Metroid Dread, and Skull & Bones.

articles.title: Resident Evil Overtakes Weapons as Zach Cregger's Highest-Grossing Film, The Social Reckoning Bombs
articles.summary: Resident Evil beat Weapons to become director Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office. The live-action adaptation of Capcom's classic survival horror series turned heads as it reached an estimated worldwide total of $320.2 million over the weekend.
body: Cregger brought his re-imagined Raccoon City to the big screen on September 18, 2026, making this weekend its fourth in theaters. The massive jump – which saw it return to the number one spot, globally – was largely propelled by its premiere in China. Of the whopping $62.65 million it accumulated through weekend four, $40.6 million was earned in China alone. Its victory over Weapons already seemed secure, but as it stands atop Cregger's catalog, it's also continuing to leave its reported $75 million budget in the dust.

Resident Evil's ongoing success in theaters kicked off when it brought in $108.3 million in its opening weekend. It was a strong start that even managed to bleed over into the gaming world with increased sales for some of the games, too, with Cregger's latest also landing as the highest-rated video game adaptation of all time.

articles.title: Steven Spielberg's Polarizing Fantasy Film Gets Official New Release
articles.summary: Steven Spielberg has spent more than five decades making movies, and his filmography is packed with classics that have become part of the cultural fabric. Jaws, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Raiders of the Lost Ark, Jurassic Park, and Schindler's List are just a handful of the films that helped…
body: Even after all these years, Spielberg's movies continue to find new audiences, whether through theatrical rereleases, streaming or upgraded home-video editions. But not every Spielberg movie has enjoyed the same level of universal acclaim. One of his most divisive movies is getting a major new release this fall, giving fans a chance to revisit one of the director's strangest and most ambitious family adventures.

Hook, Spielberg's 1991 reimagining of J.M. Barrie's Peter Pan story starring Robin Williams as a grown-up Peter Pan and Dustin Hoffman as Captain Hook, celebrates its 35th anniversary in 2026 and Sony is releasing the film as a limited-edition 4K Ultra HD SteelBook on Nov. 17.

articles.title: 8 Best Cyberpunk 2077 Replacement Games
articles.summary: If the recent re-release of The Witcher 3 gave you some Cyberpunk 2077 blues, at least know there are plenty of alternatives. Its developer, CD Projekt Red, did not invent dystopian neon, and there are many titles out there that either show up in full cyberpunk gear or have a similar feel …
body: Night City won’t let go of you easily. Nor is Cyberpunk 2077 a game you’ll soon forget. The neon and chrome aesthetic, the pervading corporate rot, and V’s Keanu-Reeves-assisted identity crisis are more than enough to build a dystopia that sticks in your mind. Once you’ve left it, you might even miss it.
What you’ll like about it: It’s rife with corporate conspiracies, it grapples with augmentation ethics, and it’s got a body arguing with its owner, too.

In Deus Ex: Mankind Divided, set in the far-off future year 2029, Adam Jensen is thrown into a mission to stop a group of rogue arms dealers from selling weapons and augmentations. Unfortunately, that mission doesn’t end well, thanks to a band of murderous mercenaries in creepy gold masks who crash the deal and turn the whole thing into a firefight.

articles.title: New NetEase FPS Sparks Warzone 'Rip-Off' Claims, But Some Call of Duty Fans Are Happy to See It
articles.summary: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.
body: NetEase called its new shooter a "self-developed extreme-sports tactical shooter" when revealing it just days ago. It's yet another big swing from the China-based tech company that boasts breakneck gameplay on PC via Steam and mobile devices, but in the hours since its big debut, it's also been called a "1:1 rip" of Activision's Call of Duty: Warzone, and it's not too hard to see why.

Viewers say guns look, kick, and move in a way that seems familiar, but the similarities don't stop there. Everything down the UI is being investigated by FPS enjoyers, too, with things like the sound effects also evoking the same kind of gritty action Call of Duty is known for. Even the way the first-person camera blurs when dropping from heights might feel familiar to fans of Warzone and other shooters. Even with characters that present their own unique abilities and gadgets, ECC: Redline has had a hard time escaping the comparisons online.
"Warzone + Delta Force + Blood Strike = ECC: Redline," one YouTube comment left on NetEase's official upload said.
points: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.

articles.title: Nintendo Should Add Wii to Switch Online Just For These 12 Classic Games
articles.summary: There’s no shortage of gems in the Wii library, and they didn’t all come from Nintendo itself. Thinking back on some of the games that people missed at the time, it’s easy to argue that Nintendo should add Wii to Switch Online sometime soon, if only so we have another chance to play classic games…
body: With GameCube games now available to play on Nintendo Switch Online with the Expansion Pack upgrade, it’s fun to think about other hardware that might benefit from similar treatment. The Wii springs most readily to mind, with a lineup of amazing games many players will remember from the system’s heyday.

Cing, a developer known for its adventure titles, had one of its most acclaimed games with Little King’s Story. Co-developed with Town Factory, the real-time strategy game lets players assume the role of a cartoon king who explores his kingdom in a quest to gain wealth and territory. Along the way, he battles monsters and completes tasks for the populace, which allows him to gain additional resources while his kingdom grows. A port is available on Steam, once again from publisher Xseed Games, but the title remains underrepresented on consoles. It would make a compelling addition to Switch Online libraries.

articles.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer's devs tested its roguelite progression system by turning it into a board game
articles.summary: Years ago, I read that Jake Solomon prototyped the Firaxis reboot of XCOM by making a simple board game version. Something rudimentary that could be played in the office on scrap paper to get ideas across and figure out where the fun would be, without having to commit.
body: As Fuse Games' creative director Kieran Crimmins told Eurogamer, "You can't know if you can feel the system until you can play the system." And so the early prototype of this high-speed arcade racing game was indeed a board game.

"You know, modern engines are so capable that you can do a lot of it in-software," CEO Matt Webster said, "but there's still something [about that which is] not as fast as getting a written idea down. From a board game perspective, you sort of decouple yourself from a particular prototype and you're talking about moment-to-moment."

Specifically, the board game simulated Galactic Racer's progression system. Its rewards differ based on the event, but typically offer tuning points to spend on one of three random stats, and maybe a part for your speeder that will affect its abilities or grant a bonus related to a specific status effect. After several races you get to go shopping, and spend the credits you've earned on more upgrades and parts, or a whole new ability.

As Fuse Games' creative director Kieran Crimmins told Eurogamer, "You can't know if you can feel the system until you can play the system.

articles.title: Seamless Landing mod looks set to bring Starfield another step closer to No Man's Sky
articles.summary: There are mods for Seamless Grav Jumps and for Seamless Planet Takeoffs. But when you arrive at a planet in Starfield you still have to choose a landing spot, and then watch a loading screen and an animation.
body: When you're in space, Starfield's planets are basically just textures you can fly right through if you put in the hours to try it, as Alanah Pearce discovered back when the RPG's boundaries were still being explored. It seemed like one gap modders would never be able to paper over, but Frederik Wessberg has apparently managed it.

The video of his work-in-progress mod shows a planetary approach, complete with heating effects on the ship during atmospheric entry, a moment of white as he hits a layer of clouds, and then the ship just lands. It seems like the clouds are there to mask a moment of loading, but Wessberg says "the cloud cover is in fact not a fancy loading screen."

body: Developer Arc System Works announced the lineup on Twitter/X, alongside artwork by Marvel artist Peach Momoko.

Phoenix Cyclops is first, arriving on 2nd November, with Classic and Legacy costumes for the character launching the same day. Thor (Jane Foster) follows in winter 2027, then Venom and a Klyntar stage in spring 2027. Jubilee is expected to drop in summer 2027.
The characters and the stage make up the Year One Characters & Stage Pass, although each can also be bought individually.
In a PlayStation Blog post, producer Takeshi Yamanaka explained why the team picked the Phoenix version of Cyclops, with new visuals, Optic Blasts, and Dark Phoenix gameplay.

articles.title: The shortlist for 2026's Golden Joystick Awards is out, including PC Game of the Year, and you can vote now
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: The Golden Joystick Awards have been running for so long there was a period where they awarded separate prizes for 8-bit and 16-bit games in each category. In 1988, rail shooter Operation Wolf was the 8-bit Computer Game of the Year, while the Bitmap Brothers' futuresport Speedball took home 16-bit Computer Game of the Year.

The shortlist of nominees in publicly voted categories for this year's 44th annual Golden Joystick Awards have been announced. (The nominees for Ultimate Game of the Year won't be revealed until October 26, when voting will open in that category too.) Of particular interest to us are the 10 games chosen for PC Game of the Year.

To qualify these games had to be released between November 1, 2025, and September 25, 2026, unless pre-release versions could be made available to the judges before the deadline. What's your pick, and is there something you think deserved to make the cut that's missing here?

articles.title: PvP pinball is such a good idea I can't believe I haven't played it before
articles.summary: One of the great things about videogame conventions is there are always people up for playing a local multiplayer game, just waiting to be handed controls and thrown into a new experience. Which is how, at PAX Australia over the weekend, I found myself playing a game called Bumper Bout.
body: Bumper Bout is two-player competitive pinball. If you know Puyo Puyo Tetris it's like that, but if you don't then imagine you're playing pinball on one half of the screen while someone else beside you is doing the same, only with the ability to flick balls across the divide. While you're trying to land a skill shot or just frantically deal with the balls already pinging between your flippers, the neighbor casually lobs another problem over the fence and says, "Deal with this. Good luck!"

Bumper Bout had the honor of being chosen as the final game of the Omegathon, the main stage tournament that plays out over the course of PAX, where it was introduced as a game made by someone who thought, "I love pinball, but no one ever dies."

Every time a ball goes down the ballhole you lose a heart, and the first player to lose five hearts loses the round. But scoring points by hitting bumpers and targets earns attack balls that you can zip over to harass your opponent, or store until you get four of them, unlocking your character's ultimate ability—which might let you create a gravity well or, if you're playing the pirate, throw bombs around the already hectic playfield.

articles.title: Escape the Backrooms is throwing an After Party with three new levels this December
articles.summary: Escape the Backrooms is adding three new levels this December, as part of a party-themed update called the After Party.
body: Publisher Secret Mode announced the news on 8th October, after the update was teased at the Triple-I Initiative showcase, the same presentation in which we learned the developer of El Paso, Elsewhere announced Gods With Badges.

The After Party is meant to bring a celebratory vibe to the co-op horror game, with new skins to dress up in alongside the new levels, so we can indulge in a little cake before running screaming from the entities that live in the Backrooms.
Before then, a selection of free and paid cosmetics is arriving in October. It sounds like you'll be able to dress up as an entity yourself, if you fancy scaring your friends.

Escape the Backrooms, from developer Fancy Games, has now been played by more than 12 million people since it launched in Early Access in 2022. It's a one to four-player co-op horror game with more than 30 levels, and is available on Steam, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. Oh, and there was that massively successful Hollywood movie, too.

articles.title: "We have to go a different path" - Krafton thinks PUBG Ded.Net's pulpy gameshow hyperviolence and roguelite twist can make it the next big battle royale
articles.summary: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade. If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.
body: Fortnite might have stolen the battle royale crown, but PUBG's name still means something even today. So when publisher Krafton announced a brand-new PUBG was in the works last month, it was an immediately exciting prospect for battle royale fans. And doubtless a daunting one for its development team, given the large shoes Ded.Net has to fill.

But what does it mean to make a new PUBG in the shadow of the original? How do you make something familiar, while keeping it fresh enough that it doesn't feel redundant? The answer may lie in Ded.Net; a grungy splatterfest being developed by Krafton's Wisconsin studio, PUBG Madison, that gives those battle royale fundamentals a more rogue-like spin. To find out more, I spoke with creative director Dave Curd about the challenges and opportunities facing the team.

"I was charged with spreading the gospel of PUBG to an audience that might not already appreciate it or like it or understand it," Curd told me at Gamescom. And that required breaking it down to its fundamentals. "What is PUBG? Is it a blue Zone? Is it the level three helmet? I think [it's] desperate survival. I think it's survival of the fittest, it's dog eat dog."
points: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade.
If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.

videos.title: Tekken 8 - Official Roger Jr. Gameplay Trailer (Ft. Yujiro Hanma Teaser)
videos.summary: Fresh from EVO France, we got the first look at everyone's favorite boxing Kangaroo, Roger Jr! Appearing for the first time since Tekken Tag Tournament 2, this feisty boxing duo excels at getting into their opponent's face and overwhelming them with offence and mixups!
body: We also got our first in-game look at Yujiro Hanma, the final DLC fighter of Season 3, with a gameplay trailer set for the Tekken World Tour Finals on January 17th 2027.
You can get boxing with Roger Jr. when the duo step into the ring for Season Pass holders on November 12th! TEKKEN 8 is out now for PlayStation 5 (PS5), PC (Steam) and Xbox Series X|S.
